speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history; the pattern of asymmetric joint involvement and urinary symptoms is very suggestive. How old are you, and when did these recent knee and urinary symptoms first begin?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive Arthritis (Reiter's Syndrome) due to Chlamydia trachomatis infection.

REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, Urine Culture, Chlamydia/Gonorrhea NAAT, HLA-B27 genetic test.
REQUEST IMAGES: X-Ray of the Right Knee and Left Ankle to assess for erosive changes or enthesitis.
